You are doing functional research for "Atlas ERP", an open-source ERP whose explicit benchmark is SAP S/4HANA. Your assigned S/4HANA area: Inventory Management & Warehousing (MM-IM / EWM).

TASK: Establish what this area actually covers in current S/4HANA (2025/2026), identify the 6-12 capabilities practitioners consider essential, and judge each against the planned Atlas v1 scope below.

METHOD: Use WebSearch (and WebFetch for promising pages) - 2 to 5 targeted searches. Prefer SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, and reputable ERP consulting sources. If web tools are unavailable or consistently fail, fall back to your embedded knowledge of S/4HANA and say so explicitly in the overview field.

COVER AT MINIMUM: Material master, stock types and movements, goods movements, physical inventory / cycle counting, material valuation (moving average, FIFO, standard), batch and serial number management; Extended Warehouse Management: storage bins, waves, handling units, putaway/picking strategies.

PLANNED ATLAS V1 SCOPE FOR THIS AREA (judge full/partial/out-of-scope against THIS, not your own ideas):
Items (stocked / non-stocked / service), lot & serial tracking, multi-UoM with conversions; multi-warehouse, multi-bin; stock moves as the single source of truth for every change; moving average AND FIFO costing per item category; COGS auto-posted via events; reorder points -> auto-draft requisitions; physical/cycle counts with variance posting. EWM waves, handling units and strategy engines are not in the v1 list.

RULES:
- atlas_v1 = "full" when Atlas v1 plans the practitioner-essential core of the capability; "partial" when a meaningful but reduced subset is planned; "out-of-scope" when none of it is planned.
- Every "partial" and "out-of-scope" entry MUST have a non-empty reason (why cut / where the boundary sits) and later_path (how to add it later in one line).
- atlas_module must be one of: finance, inventory, procurement, sales, manufacturing, quality, maintenance, hr, projects, crm, reporting, admin, industry, core, frontend, or "-" for out-of-scope.
- Be honest: if S/4HANA has an essential capability the Atlas plan misses entirely, include it as out-of-scope rather than omitting it.

Your final output is consumed by a script - return only the structured data.

## Key Capabilities of SAP S/4HANA Inventory Management (MM-IM)

### Goods Movements
The core goods movement processes include: Goods Receipt (GR) when materials are received and stock is increased, Goods Issue (GI) when materials are issued for production/sales and stock decreases, Stock Transfer for moving materials between plants or storage locations, and Transfer Posting for reclassifying stock between types.

### Physical Inventory
Physical Inventory involves manual counting and reconciliation of stock to match system records. Key processes include execution of stock transfer posting and physical inventory.

### Material Valuation
The system helps with real-time valuation and inventory management using standard price, moving average, and FIFO methods, ensuring organisations have an accurate view of their inventory and assisting with cost control and financial reporting.

### Real-Time Capabilities
The system offers live inventory status that allows you to monitor stock levels, availability, and material movements in real-time. With SAP S/4HANA, inventory management is more agile and real-time.

### Advanced Optimization Tools
The module offers advanced inventory optimization tools, such as safety stock planning, reorder point planning, and service level optimization, helping maintain the optimal balance between inventory costs and service levels.

### User Interface
SAP S/4HANA Inventory Management leverages the SAP Fiori interface, a modern and user-friendly design that provides role-based access and personalized dashboards.

Based on the search results, here's comprehensive information about SAP S/4HANA Extended Warehouse Management (EWM) core features:

## Overview

Extended Warehouse Management (EWM) offers flexible, automated support for processing various goods movements and for managing stocks in your warehouse complex, supporting planned and efficient processing of all logistics processes in your warehouse.

## Core Features and Capabilities

### Storage and Warehouse Structure

You can set up different storage facilities such as automatic warehouses, high-rack storage areas, bulk storage areas, or fixed bin warehouses, in various storage types, according to your requirements. You manage the stocks at storage bin level, and you can define these storage bins according to your own requirements.

### Advanced Operational Features

EWM manages the entire process with incredible detail including: Labor Management (tracking how long tasks take), Wave Management (organizing picking for multiple orders simultaneously), Slotting (optimizing where products should be stored based on demand), Value-Added Services (VAS) (managing kitting or special packaging), and Advanced RF/Mobile Functionality (modern, user-friendly mobile interfaces).

### Putaway and Picking Strategies

EWM optimizes warehouse capacities and material flows using putaway and stock removal strategies that you can adjust to your needs, or by you using handling units.

### Goods Movement Processing

You process all goods movements that affect your warehouse using EWM, such as goods receipts, goods issues, stock transfers, and automatic replenishment, including goods receipts, goods issues, stock transfers, automatic replenishment, and management of dangerous goods.

### Inbound and Outbound Operations

EWM supports advanced inbound and outbound processes, such as value-added services (VAS), kitting, cross-docking, and yard management, enabling more efficient goods receipt, putaway, order picking, packing, and goods issue processes.

### Advanced Features

The system expands AI capabilities available for SAP EWM, adds more functionalities and scenarios for Advanced Shipping & Receiving integration, delivers extensibility and user experience improvements, and improves Quality Management and Production integrations.

I've completed the web search. Here are the key findings related to your query about S/4HANA material master concepts:

## Material Valuation and Price Control

In Transaction-Based material price determination, with price control V, materials are valued at the moving average price, while with price control S, materials are valued at the standard price. Standard Price (S) is fixed with variances posted to a price difference account, while Moving Average Price (V) changes dynamically with each procurement.

## Material Ledger

In SAP S/4HANA, Material Ledger is on by default (built-in). The material ledger is a tool that collects data for materials for which master data is stored in the material master, and uses this data to calculate prices for valuating materials. Material Ledger is mandatory in S/4HANA and records all material valuations, actual costing, and currency conversions.

## Batch and Serial Number Management

The module enables you to manage materials in batches, allowing you to track and trace products based on attributes like manufacturing date, expiration date, and quality specifications, with batch management helping to ensure product quality and compliance. The module supports serial number management, allowing you to track individual items throughout their lifecycle, and you can assign serial numbers during goods receipt, production, or sales processes.

## Stock Types and Special Stock

Valuation levels (plant, batch, serial number) for materials can be defined using transaction OMS2.

input.overview: In current S/4HANA (2025), MM-IM covers the material/product master, all goods movements (GR, GI, transfer postings, stock transfers) recorded in the unified MATDOC table, stock types and special stocks, physical inventory with cycle counting, and material valuation through the now-mandatory Material Ledger (standard price, moving average, FIFO/balance-sheet valuation), plus batch and serial number management and reorder-point replenishment. Warehousing is handled by embedded or decentralized EWM, whose basic tier covers storage-type/bin structures, putaway and stock-removal strategies, and handling units, while waves, slotting, labor management and MFS sit in the advanced (separately licensed) tier. Findings come from live web research (SAP Help Portal, SAP Learning, SAP Community, SAP PRESS and ERP consulting sources), cross-checked against embedded knowledge. Atlas v1 covers the transactional inventory core well (moves as single source of truth, MAV+FIFO costing, counts, lot/serial, reorder points) but deliberately stops short of stock-status/special-stock dimensions, standard costing, and the EWM execution layer (strategies, waves, handling units).

capabilities.capability: Material / product master with item types and multi-UoM
capabilities.description: Central material record (basic, purchasing, sales, MRP, accounting views) with material types and unit-of-measure conversions driving all logistics and valuation.
capabilities.later_path: Richer attribute views (classification, plant-specific MRP data) can be layered onto the item entity later.

capabilities.capability: Goods movements with movement types (GR, GI, transfer posting, stock transfer)
capabilities.description: Every stock change is a goods movement document (unified MATDOC in S/4HANA) that updates quantity and value in real time and drives FI postings.

capabilities.capability: Stock types and special stocks (unrestricted / QI / blocked; consignment, subcontracting, in-transit)
capabilities.description: Stock carries a usability status and ownership category so the same quantity can be quality-inspection, blocked, vendor consignment, at-subcontractor, or in transit.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 tracks quantity per warehouse/bin via stock moves but plans no stock-status dimension (QI/blocked) and no special-stock ownership categories such as consignment or subcontractor stock.
capabilities.later_path: Add status and ownership dimensions to stock quants/move lines, with status-change moves reusing the existing move ledger.

capabilities.capability: Physical inventory and cycle counting with difference posting
capabilities.description: Periodic, continuous and cycle-count procedures: create count documents, enter counts, post differences as valued goods movements reconciled to FI.
capabilities.later_path: Sampling-based inventory and ABC-driven count scheduling can be added on top of the count engine later.

capabilities.capability: Material valuation: moving average, standard price, FIFO (Material Ledger)
capabilities.description: Mandatory Material Ledger values every movement; price control S (standard, with price-difference variances) or V (moving average), plus FIFO/balance-sheet valuation and actual costing.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans moving average AND FIFO per item category with event-driven COGS posting, but omits standard costing with variance (price-difference) postings, which manufacturers treat as essential.
capabilities.later_path: Add a standard-cost method to the per-item-category costing engine, posting purchase/production variances to dedicated variance accounts.

capabilities.description: Lot-level tracking with batch master, expiry/shelf-life data and traceability, plus serial numbers tracking individual units across receipt, stock and issue.
capabilities.later_path: Automatic batch determination (FEFO, characteristics-based selection) and shelf-life blocking can be added as picking-time rules later.

capabilities.description: Reorder-point and safety-stock planning monitors stock levels and automatically generates procurement proposals (requisitions) when stock falls below threshold.
capabilities.later_path: Full MRP (time-phased, BOM-driven) belongs to a later manufacturing module; v1 reorder-point-to-draft-requisition covers the inventory-side core.

capabilities.capability: Warehouse structure: warehouses, storage types/sections, storage bins and quants
capabilities.description: EWM models a warehouse as storage types, sections, activity areas and bins with capacity attributes; stock is managed as quants at bin level.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans multi-warehouse and multi-bin stock keeping, but only a flat warehouse-to-bin model: no storage-type/section hierarchy, capacity checks, or activity areas.
capabilities.later_path: Introduce an optional storage-type/zone layer and capacity attributes on bins without changing the move ledger.

capabilities.description: Rule engines that determine the optimal bin for putaway (e.g. fixed bin, next empty bin, bulk) and for picking (e.g. FIFO, FEFO, partial-quantity-first).
capabilities.reason: Explicitly excluded from Atlas v1: bins are chosen manually on stock moves; no strategy engine suggests or enforces source/destination bins.
capabilities.later_path: Add a rule-based bin-determination service invoked at stock-move creation, starting with fixed-bin and FIFO/FEFO rules.

capabilities.capability: Wave management and warehouse task/order processing
capabilities.description: Groups outbound picking work into waves and breaks execution into warehouse tasks/orders assigned to resources for high-volume fulfillment.
capabilities.reason: Explicitly excluded from v1; Atlas moves are executed directly with no intermediate task/wave layer. In SAP this is an advanced-EWM (extra license) feature, so it is not basic-tier core.
capabilities.later_path: Introduce a warehouse-task layer between documents and stock moves, then add wave grouping and release rules on top.

capabilities.capability: Handling unit management (packing, nested HUs, SSCC labeling)
capabilities.description: Manages packed units (pallet/carton with packaging material + contents) as single objects through receiving, putaway, picking and shipping, including nesting and SSCC identification.
capabilities.reason: Explicitly excluded from Atlas v1; stock is tracked as loose quantities per bin with no pack/container object, even though HU management is part of SAP's basic EWM tier and core for shipping-heavy operations.
capabilities.later_path: Add an HU entity that wraps stock quants with pack/unpack/move-HU operations reusing the existing stock-move ledger.

content.text: Research complete. The structured output has been returned with 11 capabilities assessed against the Atlas v1 scope: 5 full (goods movements, material master, physical inventory, batch/serial, reorder points), 3 partial (stock types/special stocks, valuation missing standard costing, flat warehouse structure), and 3 out-of-scope (putaway/picking strategies, waves, handling units).
